answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the dune schedule in the ocean ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the anchor checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 103 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 3 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
